issues.failure_explanation: The proof rewrites [B,(x+y)gamma]^T[B,(x+y)gamma] as diag(B^TB,1) + [[0,gamma B^Ty],[gamma y^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2]], whose bottom-right entry is 1+gamma^2||x+y||^2, not the correct gamma^2||x+y||^2 of the immediately preceding (correct) decomposition. It then replaces lambda_max(diag(B^TB,1)) = max(sigma_max^2(B),1) by sigma_max^2(B) and lambda_min(diag(B^TB,1)) = min(sigma_min^2(B),1) by sigma_min^2(B); with the correct decomposition the Weyl lower bound uses lambda_min(diag(B^TB,0)) = 0, never sigma_min^2(B). The stated bounds are false: item 1 with B=[1;0], x=(0,1), y=0, gamma=1e-3 gives kappa([B,b])=1000 while the bound is about 1.0000005; item 2 fails even for unit-norm columns and kappa(B)=1: B=[e1,e2] in R^{3x2}, x=e3, y=0.9e1 gives ||B^Ty||/||x+y|| = 0.6689 = (eps^2-1)/4 with eps about 1.917, and kappa([B,(x+y)/||x+y||]) is about 2.245 > kappa(B)*sqrt(1+f(B,eps)) which is about 2.131. (The step 'sqrt(1+4||B^Ty||^2/||x+y||^2) <= eps' also does not follow from the stated hypothesis, which only gives eps^2 >= 1+4r, not 1+4r^2.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No local edit preserves the stated formulas. A correct version must restate the bounds, e.g. sigma_max^2([B,b]) <= max(sigma_max^2(B), gamma^2||x+y||^2) + gamma||B^Ty|| and sigma_min^2([B,b]) >= min(sigma_min^2(B), gamma^2||x+y||^2) - gamma||B^Ty|| via Weyl applied to the correct block decomposition. This changes the form of the bounds, admits a nonpositive denominator, and abandons item 2's closed kappa(B)*sqrt(1+f(B,eps)) form, which is false even under unit-norm columns.
issues.overall_effect: Both items of the section's theorem, the advertised assumption-free foundation of the paper and the prose claim that it extends Theorem 2.3 of Liesen et al., are unreliable. No later labelled result cites thm:cool, so the failure is contained to Section 3.
issues.title: Theorem thm:cool's growth bounds are false: wrong Gram-matrix decomposition and invalid Weyl bound for sigma_min
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated, with explicit counterexamples in its target regimes; every source-supported resolution changes the content of the bounds and requires a new statement and proof, so a substantive result is abandoned even though nothing downstream depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking alpha -> 0 in the integral definition via I_{M-1}(alpha x) ~ (alpha x/2)^{M-1}/Gamma(M) gives Q^ma_M(0,beta) = Gamma(M, beta^2/2)/Gamma(M): the integrand becomes x^{2M-1} e^{-x^2/2}/(2^{M-1} Gamma(M)) and the integral equals 2^{M-1} Gamma(M, beta^2/2). The stated special case Gamma(M,beta^2)/Gamma(M) contradicts this (e.g., M=1: the integral gives e^{-beta^2/2}, the special case gives e^{-beta^2}). Hence formulas evaluating the alpha=0 case compute tail probabilities at sqrt(2)*eps: 1 - Q^ma_{m/2}(0, eps/sigma) equals P(chi^2_m <= 2 eps^2/sigma^2) = P(||Y|| <= sqrt(2) eps), not P(||Y|| <= eps).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Gamma(M,beta^2) by Gamma(M,beta^2/2) in the alpha=0 special case; all subsequent statements then read correctly.
issues.overall_effect: The definition is internally incompatible, and cor:golden2 and cor:golden3, as written with this definition, are quantitatively wrong by a factor of 2 in the incomplete-gamma argument.
issues.title: Marcum-Q special case at alpha=0 inconsistent with the integral definition (beta^2 instead of beta^2/2)
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction restores consistency of the definition and makes every dependent formula read correctly; no inference or claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $X\in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $Y$ is a random vector such that $Y_i$s are i.i.d. and $Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, then:
This result follows directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:Malcum-Bessel} by setting $X=0$ and applying basic probability theory.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion ||Y||^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_m requires independence of the components; the corollary assumes only marginal normality. Counterexample: Y_1 = ... = Y_m ~ N(0,sigma^2) (perfectly correlated) gives ||Y||^2 = m Y_1^2, a scaled chi^2_1, so P(||Y|| <= eps) differs from 1 - Q^ma_{m/2}(0, eps/sigma). The proof ('follows directly from Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel') needs that theorem's i.i.d. hypothesis, which is not assumed.

failure_location.quote: If $Y\in \mathbb{R}^m$ is a random vector such that $Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, then:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add that the Y_i are i.i.d., matching the hypothesis of Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary is false for dependent components with the same marginals; it is not used downstream, so the effect is confined to the statement.
issues.title: cor:golden2 omits the i.i.d. hypothesis on the components of Y
issues.why_classification: Adding the omitted standard independence hypothesis is a forced local condition; the conclusion, method, and all uses survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \( Q \) be an orthonormal \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.failure_explanation: P_B^\perp projects onto the orthogonal complement of the column space, whose dimension is m - rank(B), not m - n. The Marcum order (m-n)/2 is correct only when rank(B) = n. Counterexample: B = 0 (m x n) gives P_B^\perp = I, so ||P_B^\perp(Y)||^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_m, not chi^2_{m-n}. The result reduces to Theorem thm:projected-noise, which requires an orthonormal m x n Q, i.e., rank n.

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \), and \( Y \in \mathbb{R}^m \) be a random vector with i.i.d. components \( Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2) \). Then:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that B has full column rank (or replace n by rank(B) in the Marcum order).
issues.overall_effect: The stated formula is wrong for rank-deficient B (wrong Marcum order). Its later use inside the proof of thm:noise-ls concerns a full-rank matrix A and is unaffected.
issues.title: cor:golden3 omits the full-column-rank hypothesis on B
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard full-rank condition is a forced local fix; the method, conclusion, and advertised scope all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $Z_1 \sim \chi^2_n$, $Z_2 \sim \chi'^2_{m-n}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2^2}{\sigma^2}\right)$, therefore, by Chapter 6, equation 40 of \cite{patnaik1949non}, we have:

issues.failure_explanation: Z_1 = ||P_Q Y|| and Z_2 = ||X + P_Q^\perp Y|| are norms, so Z_1^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_n and Z_2^2/sigma^2 ~ chi'^2_{m-n}(||X||^2/sigma^2); the noncentral F variable is (Z_2^2/(m-n))/(Z_1^2/n), not (Z_2/(m-n))/(Z_1/n) as asserted via Patnaik (a ratio of chi variables is not F-distributed). Consequently P(Z_1/Z_2 <= eps_1/eps_2) equals the noncentral-F tail at n eps_2^2/((m-n) eps_1^2): the argument must be squared. As stated, e.g., eps_2 = 2 eps_1 evaluates the tail at 2n/(m-n) instead of 4n/(m-n). (F' is also never defined; the proof uses it both as the distribution and as the complementary CDF.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the distributional step to the ratio of scaled chi-square variables, (Z_2^2/(m-n))/(Z_1^2/n) ~ F'_{m-n,n}(||X||^2/sigma^2), define F' as the noncentral-F complementary CDF, and square the argument: F'_{m-n,n}(n eps_2^2/((m-n) eps_1^2); ||X||^2/sigma^2); propagate the square to cor-main and cor:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central least-squares-under-noise probability formula is quantitatively wrong, and the probability guarantees of cor-main and cor:added-2 repeat the same unsquared argument.
issues.title: thm:noise-ls: noncentral-F tail formula has unsquared argument; proof treats chi variables as chi-square
issues.why_classification: The repair fixes a genuinely false distributional inference and changes the functional dependence of the main probability formula and of two dependents (squaring eps_2/eps_1), but it preserves the form of the result and requires no new proof architecture or loss of guarantee type.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \), \( c\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), \( \gamma \in \mathbb{R} \), \( B = QR \), and \( \alpha=1+\gamma^2\|c\|_2^2 \).
Let $B = QR$ be a QR-factorization of the matrix $B$, and let $\gamma > 0$ be a real parameter.

Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( c\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), \( \gamma \in \mathbb{R} \), and \( \alpha=1+\gamma^2 \|c\|_2^2 \). If \( \|r\|_2=\min_{z}\{c\gamma-Bz\} \), then:

issues.failure_explanation: Since [B,c gamma] = [Q,c] diag(R, gamma), the relevant norms are max(sigma_max(R), |gamma|) and min(sigma_min(R), |gamma|). With gamma < 0, item thm:min-max-cond-1 is false: B = Q = [1;0], c = (0,1), gamma = -100 give sigma_max([B,c gamma]) = 100 but the stated bound is max(sigma_max(B), gamma) sigma_max([Q,c]) = 1. The cited Liesen theorem (thm:strak) assumes gamma > 0 and r != 0, but thm:min-max-cond and thm:lm:cond-ls state gamma in R, and lm:cond-ls/cor:cond-ls also drop r != 0 although they divide by gamma ||r||: for gamma < 0 the right-hand side of lm:cond-ls is negative while kappa >= 1, and r = 0 leaves the formulas undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume gamma > 0 in thm:min-max-cond and thm:lm:cond-ls (equivalently, replace gamma by |gamma| in the max/min factors and in the final denominator), and add the hypothesis r != 0 in thm:lm:cond-ls and cor:cond-ls.
issues.overall_effect: Items 1-3 of thm:min-max-cond are false or vacuous for gamma < 0, and the bounds of thm:lm:cond-ls and cor:cond-ls are false or undefined outside gamma > 0, r != 0. Every application in the paper uses gamma = 1 > 0 and r > 0 almost surely.
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond and lm:cond-ls quantify over gamma in R and drop r != 0; bounds fail for gamma < 0
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypotheses gamma > 0 and r != 0 is a local forced condition; every advertised application (gamma = 1, r > 0 a.s.) and all conclusions and rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The two expressions are different bounds and are not equal. Counterexample: B = Q = [1;0] (so kappa(B) = ||B|| = ||B^dagger|| = 1), c = (1,1)/sqrt(2), gamma = 2: the first form is max{1,1,1}*kappa([Q,2c]) = kappa([[1,sqrt(2)],[0,sqrt(2)]]) which is about 3.226, while the second form is max{1,1/2,2}*kappa([Q,c]) = 2*2.414 which is about 4.828. Each side is separately a valid upper bound for kappa([B,c gamma]) (the first via [B,c gamma] = [Q,c gamma] diag(R,1) with kappa(diag(R,1)) <= max{kappa(B),||B||,||B^dagger||}; the second via the proof's max/min identity, which is correct), but the proof derives only the second form and never the first, and the displayed '=' between them is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the two bounds as separate inequalities and add the short proof of the first form: kappa([B,c gamma]) <= kappa(diag(R,1)) kappa([Q,c gamma]) <= max{kappa(B), ||B||_2, ||B^dagger||_2} kappa([Q,c gamma]).
issues.overall_effect: The stated item asserts an identity that does not hold, so the statement claims more than the proof establishes; thm:lm:cond-ls invokes the first form, which is true but unproven in the paper.
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond item 3 chains a false equality between two different condition-number bounds
issues.why_classification: Both sides are valid upper bounds and the form used downstream is true; deleting the false equality and inserting a routine three-line argument preserves every substantive claim and guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $r \neq 0$ is the residual of the least squares problem ($\|r\|_2 = \min_{u} \|c - Bu\|_2$)

issues.failure_explanation: In the cited Theorem 2.3 (thm:strak), r is the residual of the unscaled system, ||r|| = min_u ||c - Bu||, and the formula contains gamma ||r||. thm:lm:cond-ls defines ||r|| = min_z ||c gamma - Bz|| = gamma times that residual, but then substitutes it into the same formula. For gamma != 1 the bound is wrong: B = Q = [1;0], c = (sqrt(0.99), 0.1), gamma = 2 gives a stated bound of about 12.42 while kappa([B,c gamma]) is about 24.9; for larger gamma (e.g., c = e2, gamma = 10) the discriminant alpha^2 - 4 gamma^2 ||r||^2 = 10201 - 40000 is negative, so the bound is not even defined. With the scaled residual the correct formula has no gamma factors: (alpha + sqrt(alpha^2 - 4||r||^2))/(2||r||).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define r as the residual of the unscaled system, ||r||_2 = min_z ||c - Bz||_2, matching the cited theorem; equivalently, keep the scaled residual and remove the gamma factors from the formula.
issues.overall_effect: The general-gamma 'final result' is false or undefined for gamma != 1. Its only downstream use sets gamma = 1 (cor:cond-ls), where the two residuals coincide, so cor:cond-ls, cor-main, and cor:added-2 are unaffected.
issues.title: thm:lm:cond-ls plugs the residual of c gamma into Liesen's formula, which is stated for the residual of c
issues.why_classification: A forced local correction (redefine r, or drop the gamma factors) makes the general-gamma statement correct and leaves all advertised gamma = 1 results and guarantees intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.

issues.failure_explanation: On the event ||r|| >= t0 := 1/sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2), monotonicity of g(t) = (1+sqrt(1-t^2))/t in cor:cond-ls gives the multiplier g(t0) = eps_1/eps_2 + sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) >= 1. The stated multiplier eps_1 sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) is strictly smaller and can be below 1: e.g., eps_1 = eps_2 = 1 gives sqrt(2) about 1.414, while ||r|| in (0.707, 0.943) - a positive-probability part of the same event - forces kappa([B,q])/kappa(B) up to 1+sqrt(2) about 2.414; concentrating Z_1/Z_2 near 0.8 makes the stated bound fail on almost the whole event while the assigned probability stays positive. For eps_1 << eps_2 the claimed multiplier tends to 0 although kappa([B,q]) >= kappa(B) always. (The statement also never defines q; the intended q = (X+Y)/||X+Y|| is visible only from the proof and cor:added-2.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the multiplier by g(t0) = eps_1/eps_2 + sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) = (eps_1 + sqrt(eps_1^2+eps_2^2))/eps_2, and define q := (X+Y)/||X+Y|| in the statement; the telescoping architecture and the type of probability guarantee are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The per-column growth bound of cor-main is false as stated, and cor:added-2's final product bound inherits the wrong factor, which can even be smaller than 1 <= kappa(Q-hat) on events assigned positive probability.
issues.title: cor-main's multiplier eps_1 sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) is wrong; the stated bound can undercut kappa(B)
issues.why_classification: The correction changes the advertised growth factor (removing impossible sub-1 bounds) and requires recomputing the threshold evaluation, but it preserves the overall proof architecture and leaves a recognizably comparable bound.

issues.failure_explanation: At iteration i the previously computed matrix Q-hat[:,1:i-1] has i-1 columns, so cor-main must be applied with n replaced by i-1: the per-step probability is F'_{m-i+1, i-1}((i-1) eps_{2,i}^2/((m-i+1) eps_{1,i}^2); ||a_i||^2/sigma^2). The stated F'_{m-i, i}(i eps_2/((m-i) eps_1); ...) has both degrees-of-freedom parameters off by one (e.g., at i = 2 the relevant complement has dimension m-1, not m-2, and ||P_Q Y||^2 has i-1 = 1 degrees of freedom, not 2). The missing square in the argument is the separate thm:noise-ls defect, and the epsilons should carry the index i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shift the parameters to m-i+1 and i-1 (and write eps_{1,i}, eps_{2,i}), i.e., apply cor-main with n -> i-1; a forced index correction.
issues.overall_effect: The probability guarantee of the paper's final corollary is quantitatively wrong even after the inherited square and multiplier errors are repaired.
issues.title: cor:added-2 uses wrong noncentral-F parameters at iteration i (m-i, i instead of m-i+1, i-1)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, forced index shift; the method, the form of the probability guarantee, and the advertised scope of the final corollary all survive.
